key_insight: Machine-learned molecular dynamics predicts that approximately 0.5% biaxial tensile strain drives MAPbI₃ from tetragonal to cubic at 300 K while retaining preferential molecular orientations.
engineering_relevance: Finite-temperature strain modeling can guide epitaxial perovskite design by predicting structural transitions and strain-dependent band gaps that static calculations miss.
method: Train machine-learned force fields on-the-fly using DFT.
Run nanosecond-long bulk and free-standing slab simulations with fixed in-plane lattice vectors.
Track octahedral tilts and lattice ratios; average band gaps over MD snapshots.
evidence_signal: The predicted transition agrees with epitaxial MAPbI₃/KCl experiments, bulk and slab models show consistent trends, and ensemble-averaged band gaps reproduce the experimental tensile-strain blue shift.
watch_item: Free-standing slabs do not explicitly capture substrate interfaces, so interface-specific effects require additional validation.
paper_title: Strain-Induced Tetragonal-to-Cubic Transition in MAPbI$_3$ from Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics
